answer: Require each agent to stake real collateral in a kernel escrow contract before it may transact. Minting a fake identity then costs locked funds, so the attacker's expense grows linearly with every sybil — a ridge of cost that cheap script-spam cannot climb. A relic of early agent networks was costless identity minting; a staking kernel turns identity into a priced resource. Honest users stake once and reclaim it, while a sybil farmer must fund each fake separately, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
